---
title: "SimilaritySearchEngine.jl"
subtitle: "An embedded similarity search engine for Julia, and the service layer built on it"
lang: en-US
---

This site documents one repository that contains two packages. They are developed, tested and
released together. The division between them is the following:

| | `SimilaritySearchEngine` | `SimilaritySearchServer` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| location | the repository root | `server/` |
| function | an embedded, in-process library: storage, indexing and search | a REST API, two command lines, and an asynchronous job queue |
| defined concepts | RocksDB column families, inverted files, proximity graphs | HTTP status codes, exit codes, job spools, access tokens |
| undefined concepts | HTTP, processes, tokens | index construction and storage |

Storage, indexing and search are implemented in the engine. The server calls the engine's
public API and does not use its internal modules. The engine contains no reference to HTTP
status codes or to process exit codes.

This separation determines how failures are reported. The engine raises a typed error, and the
category of that error states the nature of the failure. Each interface then maps the category
to its own vocabulary: HTTP status codes, command-line exit codes, or a branch in a Julia
program.

---

## Choosing a package

**To search within a Julia process, use the engine.** It requires a working directory, a
project handle, and function calls. No server process, network port or serialization is
involved. Access control is provided by the file permissions of the working directory.

: Begin with [Getting started](tutorials/getting-started.qmd), then read
[Architecture](architecture.qmd).

**To provide search to other processes, machines or programming languages, use the server.**
It holds one `EmbeddedEngine` per dataset, and translates each request into one engine call. An
operation over an entire collection is executed in a separate Julia subprocess, so that a query
is not delayed by a long operation such as `allknn`.

: Begin with the [server tutorial](server/tutorial.qmd), then read the
[server manual](server/manual.qmd).

Both packages are documented in one generated reference:
[Engine API](https://sadit.github.io/SimilaritySearchEngine.jl/api/engine.html) and
[Server API](https://sadit.github.io/SimilaritySearchEngine.jl/api/server.html).

---

## Installation

Neither package is registered in the Julia General registry, so both are installed from this
repository. The dependencies of the engine are registered:
[SimilaritySearch.jl](https://github.com/sadit/SimilaritySearch.jl),
[TextSearch.jl](https://github.com/sadit/TextSearch.jl),
[RocksDB.jl](https://github.com/sadit/RocksDB.jl), and the `RocksDB_jll` binaries. No other
repository has to be cloned, and the RocksDB binaries are not compiled here:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/sadit/SimilaritySearchEngine.jl")
```

The server is the `server/` subdirectory of the same repository, and it resolves the engine
by path:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/sadit/SimilaritySearchEngine.jl
cd SimilaritySearchEngine.jl
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.develop(path="."); Pkg.instantiate()'
julia --project=server -t auto -m SimilaritySearchServer serve
```

Both packages require Julia 1.12 or later. No `Manifest.toml` is committed for the engine, so
`Pkg.instantiate()` resolves the base libraries from the registry unless they are also
developed by path.

---

## Engine functionality

- **Project lifecycle**: `create_project`, `open_project` and `close_project!` manage the on-disk RocksDB directory and the associated search engine.
- **Separation of engine and backend**:
  - **Payload engines**: `DenseEngine`, `SparseEngine` and `FullTextEngine` determine the type of data stored.
  - **Index backends**: `SearchGraph`, `ExhaustiveSearch`, `InvertedFile` and `BM25InvertedFile` determine the indexing data structure.
  - `payload_kind(engine)` reports the data type, and the `BACKENDS` registry restricts which engine-backend pairs are valid.
- **Dense vector search**: approximate nearest neighbor search with `SearchGraph`, which tunes its beam search parameters, or exact search with `ExhaustiveSearch` and `ParallelExhaustiveSearch`. For `SearchGraph`, insertion (`append_items!`) and graph construction (`index!`) are separate operations, so the caller determines when indexing latency is incurred.
- **Sparse vector search**: inverted index search (`InvertedFile`) over sparse representations encoded by the caller, of fixed dimension. The available distance functions are cosine distance over the weights and set distances (`Dist.Sets.*`) over the support of the non-zero coordinates.
- **Full-text retrieval**: lexical search with `BM25InvertedFile` or with TF-IDF weighting (`TextInvertedFile`). The first call to `index!` fits or initializes a `TextProfile` from the staged texts, which determines the vocabulary and the term weighting model.
- **Explicit text modeling**: a text project requires an `AbstractTextModelSpec`:
  - `DefaultProfile(:lang)` resolves a pre-trained language profile and refits the vocabulary frequencies against the staged corpus.
  - `BaseProfile(p)` uses an existing `TextProfile`.
  - `FitFromCorpus(cfg)` fits a profile from the staged corpus, up to `max_documents`.
  - A query accepts a `QueryPolicy`, which determines orthographic correction and query expansion.
  - `edit_correction=true`, given to `create_project` or `open_project`, also corrects a query token that is absent from the vocabulary when exactly one vocabulary token is at edit distance 1 from it.
- **Typed interface**: input is given in typed containers (`DenseItem`, `SparseItem`, `TextItem`), and queries return structured results (`SearchResult`, `StoredItem`, `ExistsResult`).
- **Logical deletion**: `delete_item!` marks a document as deleted without modifying the index. Queries return such candidates with an explicit `deleted` field.
- **Recall calibration**: `calibrate!` optimizes the beam search parameters for a set of target recall values, which `minrecall` then selects. `SearchStats` reports the number of distance computations a query performed.
- **Operations over an entire collection**: in-process execution of all-pairs nearest neighbors (`allknn`), center selection (`fft`), closest pairs (`closestpairs`), and closest pairs between two collections (`bichromatic_kclosestpairs`).
- **Persistence**: RocksDB column families for metadata and index structures, and memory-mapped files for dense vectors (`dense_vectors.mmapdb`).
- **Typed errors**: a failure raised by the engine is an `EngineError` in one of four categories (`InvalidRequest`, `NotFound`, `ConflictingState`, `StorageFailure`), so that a caller can act on a failure without interpreting its message.

## Server functionality

- **REST API**: dataset lifecycle, insertion, dense, sparse and text search with metadata
  filters, logical deletion, recall calibration, and queries over more than one dataset
  (`hybrid`, `ftsearch_group`).
- **Asynchronous jobs**: `allknn`, `fft`, `neardup`, `hsp`, `searchbatch`, `closestpair`,
  `build`, `dump` and `load` are enqueued and executed as separate Julia subprocesses. Each
  one opens its dataset in read-only mode, so the server continues to answer queries while
  they run.
- **Two command lines**: `similarity-search` operates on a working directory, and
  `similarity-search-ctl` operates on a running server over HTTP. Both can be installed as
  applications with `Pkg.Apps`.
- **Operational interfaces**: access tokens, an operation log per dataset (whose
  distance-computation counts are obtained from the engine's `SearchStats`), cursors for
  paginated results, health and metrics endpoints, and unload and reload of a single dataset
  without restarting the server.
- **One error vocabulary**: the engine's four categories are mapped to HTTP status codes and
  to command-line exit codes by category, not by message text.
